full_judgment: 10. On the other hand Mr. A.F.M. Shahid, the learned counsel appearing for the Respondent No. 5, submits that no question of violation of the principle of natural juctice does involve in this case since the petitioner did not acquire any vested right in his favour in the incomplete election, what has been infringed by the impugned direction, issued by the Election Commission, who are under the legal obligations to see that an election has been conducted homestly, justly and fairly and in accordance with the Rules by the election machineries. Mr. Shahid further submits that the admitted incomplete election did not vest any right in favour of either of the contestant, the violation of which may legally be questioned in this writ petition. Mr. Shahid also submits that the very purpose of incorporating Rule 70 in the Election Rules is to cloth such a high ranking institution, like the Election commission with unfettered power and authority to carry out the purpose of holding election honestly, justly and fairly and in accordance with the Ordinance and the Rules framed there under. It a elucidating his submissions Mr. Shahid further submits that the Rule 70 in letters and spirit has the over ridding effect on the other Rules since no express limitation has been put in the Rule regarding the exercise of plenary power by the Election Commission for organizing, holding and conducting the elections under the Ordinance and Rules. According to Mr. Shahid vesting with such absolute power in. the Election Commission can reasonably and clearly be gathered from using of the words "honestly, justly and fairly," and as such the actions to be taken by the election machineries under the Rules have been made subordinate to the satisfaction of the Election Commission, that is to say, subject to the approval of the Election commission.
